errors.forbidden: Your platform role is not allowed to do that.
errors.scope_forbidden: Global macros are managed by platform administrators; keep this one personal.
errors.generic: That did not work. Please try again.

fieldErrors.hostname: Enter a domain name such as support.example.com (no scheme, no path).
fieldErrors.timezone: Unknown time zone — use an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin.
fieldErrors.time: Enter start and end as HH:MM.
fieldErrors.window: The end must be after the start.
fieldErrors.scope: Only platform administrators create global macros.
fieldErrors.overlap: A tag cannot be added and removed by the same macro.
fieldErrors.too_many: Too many tags — at most ten per list.

list.intro: Canned answers with optional actions. Global macros are available to every operator and managed by administrators; personal macros are yours alone. Applying a macro fills the reply editor of a ticket — nothing is sent unseen.
list.searchHint: Press <kbd>/</kbd> to jump to the search field; Escape clears it.
list.resultsFiltered: {count} of {total, plural, one {# macro} other {# macros}} match
list.caption: Macros by category and name
list.emptyText: Create your first macro: a name, the text with placeholders and, if you like, the actions it applies to the ticket.
list.emptyFilteredText: Widen the search or reset the filters.
list.readOnlyHint: This global macro is managed by platform administrators. You can apply it from any ticket's reply editor; only administrators change its text or actions.

editor.intro: Name, category and scope, the text with placeholders and the optional actions. The preview on the right shows the text with sample values.
editor.basicsText: How the macro appears in the picker and who can use it.
editor.name: Name
editor.nameHint: Short and recognisable, e.g. “Need more information”.
editor.categoryHint: Optional grouping for the picker, e.g. billing, onboarding. Existing categories are suggested.
editor.scopeHint: Personal macros are visible to you only; global macros to every operator.
editor.scopePersonalText: Only you see and use it.
editor.scopeGlobalText: Every operator can use it; administrators maintain it.
editor.scopeGlobalAdminOnly: Only platform administrators create global macros.
editor.bodyText: Plain text. Placeholders in curly braces are filled from the ticket when the macro is applied; anything else stays as written.
editor.placeholdersHint: Inserted at the cursor. An unknown requester name or organisation renders empty — the agent reviews the text before sending.
editor.bodyHint: Up to 8,000 characters. Greeting and sign-off are part of the text; the mail template adds the ticket footer.
editor.unresolved: Unknown placeholders stay in the text as written: {list}
editor.actionsText: Applied to the ticket together with the text. Leave everything empty for a text-only macro; the ticket workflow still decides whether a status change is allowed.
editor.assignToSelfText: The operator applying the macro becomes the assignee.
editor.previewHint: Rendered with sample values, not a real ticket.
editor.previewEmpty: The preview appears as soon as there is text.

deleteDialog.title: Delete this macro?
deleteDialog.description: “{name}” disappears from every picker. Messages that used it keep their text. This is recorded in the audit log.

overview.intro: Sender and reply domain, signature, automation, business hours and satisfaction surveys of the support desk. SLA policies are listed as stored; their editing is a separate section.
overview.businessHoursPending: Not read by the SLA clocks yet — every SLA policy carries its own hours.
overview.extraWindows: Some days carry more than one window; the form shows the first one.
overview.envOverride: Overridden by the environment variable {name}; the stored value is not in effect.
overview.notStored: Nothing has been saved yet — the values shown are the defaults of the schema.
overview.presenceText: Operators the desk saw within the last {minutes} minutes — the pool round-robin assignment will draw from.
overview.agentsOnline: {count, plural, one {# agent} other {# agents}} seen in the last {minutes} minutes

inbound.title: Inbound e-mail ledger
inbound.text: Webhook deliveries of the last {days} days by outcome, and the latest {limit} events with their ticket and — for failures — the stored error. The provider retries failed deliveries by itself.
inbound.countsLabel: Deliveries of the last {days} days by outcome
inbound.failedTitle: {count, plural, one {# inbound event failed} other {# inbound events failed}} in the last {days} days
inbound.failedText: The error column says why. Typical causes: a missing or wrong RESEND_API_KEY, the receiving API not reachable, or a database problem. The provider retries the delivery; a retry that succeeds changes the row to processed.
inbound.staleTitle: {count, plural, one {# delivery} other {# deliveries}} without an outcome
inbound.staleText: Received more than {minutes} minutes ago and never finished — the processing was interrupted. The provider's retry picks the delivery up again.
inbound.caption: Latest {limit} inbound webhook deliveries, newest first
inbound.emptyText: Nothing has reached the webhook so far. Once the reply domain receives mail, every delivery appears here with its outcome.

sla.title: SLA policies
sla.text: Targets per priority in business minutes, as stored. The default policy applies to every plan without its own policy.
sla.caption: SLA policies, default first
sla.emptyText: No policy is stored; tickets show “no SLA policy” until one exists.

overview.roundRobinActive: Round robin active — new tickets go to the agent online with the fewest open tickets
overview.roundRobinNobody: Round robin selected — nobody online right now, new tickets stay unassigned

general.intro: Sender, reply domain, signature, automatic acknowledgement, assignment, business hours and satisfaction survey. Every change is recorded in the audit log.
general.senderText: How ticket mails leave the desk and where replies come back.
general.fromNameHint: Shown as the sender of every ticket mail.
general.fromAddressHint: Must be on a domain verified for sending.
general.inboundDomainHint: Replies go to support+t<number>@<domain>; the domain needs an MX record and the inbound webhook.
general.envOverride: Overridden by the environment variable {name}: mails use {value}. The stored value is kept for when the variable is removed.
general.signatureHint: Appended below the agent's name on replies; up to {max} characters. Not used on automatic messages.
general.autoReplyText: Confirms a new ticket to the requester with its number. Never sent in reply to automatic messages (out of office, bounces, lists).
general.autoReplyEnabled: Send an acknowledgement for new tickets
general.autoReplyEnabledText: In the requester's language, marked as automatic so other desks do not answer it.

preview.title: Acknowledgement preview
preview.text: Built from the saved settings for a sample ticket #{number} from {name}, in {language}.
preview.disabled: The acknowledgement is off; this is what would be sent.
preview.subject: Subject

general.assignText: Who gets a new ticket. Nothing is guessed: without anyone online a ticket stays unassigned.
general.assignText_none: New tickets stay unassigned until someone picks them up.
general.assignText_round_robin: The agent seen within the last {minutes} minutes who holds the fewest open tickets gets the next one.
general.agentsOnline: Right now: {count, plural, one {# agent} other {# agents}} seen in the last {minutes} minutes.
general.hoursText: One window per weekday in the desk's time zone, stored with the settings.
general.hoursPending: Not read by the SLA clocks yet: every SLA policy carries its own business hours (section SLA policies) and nothing falls back to these desk hours so far. Saving them changes no due time.
general.extraWindows: More than one window is stored for {days}; the form shows the first one and saving replaces the rest.
general.csatText: Whether solved tickets ask the requester for a rating.
general.csatEnabled: Ask for a rating when a ticket is solved
general.csatEnabledText: One question with five levels and an optional comment; the answer is stored on the ticket.
general.pendingText: This schema (migration 0015) has no storage for a blocked-sender list or an auto-close interval, so the fields are not shown rather than shown without effect. They arrive with the next migration.
general.assignApplied: Applied on creation: inbound e-mail, the contact form and tickets opened in the customer dashboard pick the agent online with the fewest open tickets; nobody online → the ticket stays unassigned (nothing is guessed).
